<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e9688516cc2998ea7b4479b45755abd693452d36` — the merge of head `6b7710c9c0e97e31bc478da45b74fa5a3644acfd` into base `7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e9688516cc2998ea7b4479b45755abd693452d36 && git checkout e9688516cc2998ea7b4479b45755abd693452d36
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee 6b7710c9c0e97e31bc478da45b74fa5a3644acfd && git checkout -B drift-repro 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee && git merge --no-ff 6b7710c9c0e97e31bc478da45b74fa5a3644acfd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7f277a86f670a956dcdf677937c1894706992bee` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6d7e23820072973d6a94ed50aea519010772cf1d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/ui/duplicate-global-filter-names.ts + packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range.test.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/lazy-schema.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/conversions/refused-shapes.ts, packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, .changeset/29213-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range.md, .changeset/29023-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name.md, content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx, skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md, packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/verify/src/dashboard-window.ts, ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/imported-defaults.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/node-derivation.ts, ui/packages/types/src/zod/base.zod.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/clientValidation.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/metadataError.ts, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs

Inputs: card #29213 (body, triage 6574201278, claim 6576684400, os-dev-report 6578177651), PR #29370 (body, 8-file list, net diff against merge base `5a2bdf9c`), the 62 check-runs on the head. Read-only: the cited code was read on the head tree with `git show`; nothing was built, run or re-run. The seat's rulings Q1 = A and Q2 = A and the amended claim surface (the ADR-0087 entry and the one `dashboards.mdx` sentence) are judged below as decisions, not adopted as conclusions.

Gate state on the head at review time: completed success for `Lint & Repo Gates` (and every `Lint ·` and `Type Check · source gates` / `debt ledger` job under it, including `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`), `PR-body guards`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Live E2E UI`, `Build UI Deps`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Auto Label`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `filter`. Still in progress (PENDING, not read as verdicts): `Build Core`, `Test Core` (8 shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (16 shards), `Build & E2E UI`. Skipped by their own filters: `Lint UI`, `UI Published Artifacts`, the opt-in harnesses. The combined commit status is `pending`. The design is judged below regardless; the pending families are the dev's locally reported spec/lint/metadata-protocol/ui suites and the dogfood battery, which this record does not re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set narrowing of `DashboardSchema` — right.** A dashboard whose `dateRange` is a declared object and whose `globalFilters[i]` is keyed `dateRange` (non-empty `name`, else non-empty `field`) now fails to parse, one `custom` issue per such entry at `globalFilters[i].name` or `.field`. Every in-repo door parses `DashboardSchema` whole: `metadata-type-schemas.ts` maps `dashboard` to it (the save door, draft and publish), `stack.zod.ts` uses it as the `dashboards` element (`defineStack`, `os validate`, `os build`), `verify/dashboard-window.ts` calls `DashboardSchema.safeParse`, and the console's `clientValidation.ts` loads the spec `DashboardSchema` for the dashboard editor. The changeset's "every door that parses it" is true of the tree.
2. **Conditional on a declared `dateRange` (Q1 = A) — right.** The console's `resolveDashboardFilterDefs` seeds `byName` with the built-in only `if (schema.dateRange)`, then inserts every `globalFilters` entry under `f.name || f.field` with its own `type`; the filter bar and the query side branch on `def.type` (`'dateRange'` vs `'date'`/`'text'`), never on the key. Lint's `dashboardFilterDefs` seeds the built-in only when `dateRange` is a non-null object and otherwise keys entries by `name` else `field`, so `filterBindings.dateRange` is a declared key when such an entry exists. Verify marks a dashboard without `dateRange` `not-windowed` and skips it. So on an undeclared dashboard the entry is a working filter, and refusing it would take a capability away that no consumer breaks on. Adding `dateRange` later turns the pair into the refused shape, which is the loud failure the card asked for.
3. **Key derivation shared with the duplicate rule (Q2 = A) — right.** `reservedDateRangeGlobalFilters` reuses the module-private `filterKeyOf` (non-empty `name`, else non-empty `field`), the same derivation the console (`f.name || f.field`) and lint use. Exact, case-sensitive match on `'dateRange'` is what both resolvers do. Keeping it in `duplicate-global-filter-names.ts` makes the module's header true again (it no longer says `dateRange` "is not judged here"); the predicate is a second collision on the same key space, not a new class.
4. **"Declared" means any non-null object — right.** Lint tests `dateRange && typeof dateRange === 'object'`; the console tests truthiness. A string `dateRange` is refused by the schema's own `invalid_type` before the object check runs, so the predicate's `[]` for non-objects is the "left to the schema" posture the sibling predicate takes, and on a stored body it cannot mask anything the schema does not already name.
5. **Attachment on the dashboard object, not the array — right, and its reach is named correctly.** The verdict needs the sibling `dateRange`, so an array-level refine cannot carry it. The PR's acknowledged consequence holds in the tree: the UI mirror `DashboardComponentSchema` (`ui/packages/types/src/zod/complex.zod.ts`) excludes `globalFilters` from the spec fields it spreads and redefines it from the UI's own `GlobalFilterSchema`, so neither #29162's array rule nor this object rule reaches the SDUI `validateTree` path. That was already the posture after #29162; the save doors and the console editor parse the spec schema whole, so the refusal reaches every write.
6. **No published-export change.** `reservedDateRangeGlobalFilters`, `RESERVED_DATE_RANGE_FILTER_NAME` and `ReservedDateRangeGlobalFilter` are new exports of `duplicate-global-filter-names.ts`, but that module is not re-exported from `packages/spec/src/ui/index.ts` (only `dashboard.zod` and `dashboardForm` are) and appears nowhere in `api-surface/` or `export-origins/`. `refuseReservedDateRangeGlobalFilters` is module-private. The public surface change is the narrowing plus describe prose on `GlobalFilterSchema.name` and `DashboardSchema.globalFilters`, which the regenerated `content/docs/references/ui/dashboard.mdx` reflects at both sites where `GlobalFilterSchema` is printed.
7. **Dropped-refinements baseline +5 — right.** `""` is the baseline's spelling for a root-level object refinement (`ui/ListView`, `automation/Flow`, `api/CreateFlowRequest` all carry it), and `manifest.dashboards.element` on the four installed-package projections is where `stack.zod.ts` embeds the schema. 988 → 993 matches five sites. The two swapped `translations` lines are a sort-order normalisation the generator emitted; not a hits file, listed here only because the hunk is in the diff.
8. **ADR-0087 registration — right.** The changeset carries `adr-0087: registered ui-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range-refused`; the entry file `18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range-refused.ts` exports `entry` with that `id`; the registry is generated from `entries/semantic/` by `build-migration-registry.ts` (no hand edit of the template is needed or made). `Lint & Repo Gates` is green on the head.
9. **`refused-shapes.ts` untouched — right for this claim.** Neither this refusal nor #29162's duplicate-key refusal is listed there; the claim comment fences that file to sibling #29212, and the dev's `out_of_scope_findings` hands it to that carrier.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/29213-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range.md` bumps `@objectstack/spec` `minor` under `fix(spec)!:` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; the PR body carries the same three lines verbatim. That is what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing of a published schema with no exported-symbol change, which `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades `minor` with the `(narrowing)` marker during the launch window (its header: a breaking change ships as `minor`; `narrowed` beside a line without `(narrowing)` is refused). The sibling #29162 changeset (`29023-dashboard-global-filter-duplicate-name.md`, still pending in `.changeset/`) uses the identical level axis, so the two refusals of one defect class publish at one level. The `Skills-docs: none` line is true of the tree: `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md` teaches `dateRange` only as the reserved built-in (lines 12, 162, 213, 396) and no `skills/**` file keys a `globalFilters` entry `dateRange`. `Check Changeset` is green on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — correct for this diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report 6578177651):
- Two files outside the original claim surface (the ADR-0087 semantic entry; one sentence in `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`): the seat amended the claim to include both. The entry is required by the changeset's `registered` disposition and is judged under ④. The sentence is accurate against the code (refusal conditional on a declared `dateRange`, keyed by `name` else `field`, names the control and the `filterBindings.dateRange` binding it would replace); see should-fix 1 for a wording tension with the sentence above it. Accepted.
- PR body lines 1–2 are the harness attribution block, `Fixes #29213` on line 3: procedural, `PR-body guards` green. Not a contract matter.
- No MCP writes, no PR assignee, no PR-activity subscription: the standing order; nothing to escalate.
- Human Minimum item 3 (`pnpm lint`) unchecked, CI-owned: `Lint · ESLint` and `Lint · docs & code guards` are green on the head. Closed.

Open questions:
- Q1 (undeclared-`dateRange` dashboard keeps an entry keyed `dateRange`): seat ruled A. Judged right under ① item 2; the alternative would widen the refusal past the card and past what any consumer breaks on.
- Q2 (predicate placement in `duplicate-global-filter-names.ts`): seat ruled A. Judged right under ① item 3.

Out-of-scope note (`refused-shapes.ts` does not list this refusal): correctly routed to #29212, which holds that file.

Escalations: none.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/ui/duplicate-global-filter-names.ts`** — against the card's scenario and both resolvers. Tried to break it: `{ name: 'dateRange', field: 'close_date' }` is keyed by name and refused at `.name` (the card's shape); `{ field: 'dateRange' }` unnamed is keyed by field and refused at `.field` with the parenthetical the console's fallback justifies; `{ name: 'period', field: 'dateRange' }` is keyed `period` and passes, which is right because the console keys it `period` too; `{ name: '', field: 'dateRange' }` falls to the field exactly as `f.name || f.field` does; `targetWidgets` on the entry does not rescue it, right because the filter-bar control key collides regardless of which widgets it targets; two `dateRange` entries answer one reserved issue each plus the array rule's one duplicate issue, so the author sees every site. `dateRange: 'this_month'` and `null` answer `[]`, which the schema already refuses by type. The message carries no tracker number (the `check:doc-authoring` rule the test pins). The header now states the module's two predicates and their shared key space truthfully. No finding.

**`packages/spec/src/ui/dashboard.zod.ts`** — against its consumers. `strictObject(...)` returns a `closedObject` (a subclass instance); Zod 4's `.superRefine` clones through `inst.constructor(def)`, the same construction the UI's `cloneWithDef` relies on, so the surface-naming error map and terminal unknown-key refusal survive the attachment, and the result is still a `ZodObject`: `SpecDashboardSchema.shape.dateRange` (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/dashboard-filters.ts`), `DashboardSchema.shape.requiredPermissions` and the UI mirror's `stripImportedDefaults(SpecDashboardSchema).shape` keep working, since `stripImportedDefaults` walks by `_zod.def` and clones (it never calls `.extend()`), and `specFieldsExcept` builds a fresh `looseObject(...).partial()` from the shape. I searched the whole tree for `DashboardSchema.extend/omit/pick/partial/merge` and found no site, so Zod 4's refusal to `.extend()` a refined object is not reachable from this change. The lazy proxy forwards the refined instance unchanged. `z.input` / `z.output` types are unchanged. The `studio-design/metadataError.ts` `listItemHeldInput` walk sees the new issue at `globalFilters.i.name` (or `.field`) with that input set, so it classifies the item as not held and the refusal reaches the author as an ordinary field error rather than a "fill this in" prompt, which is the right reading. One observation, not a finding: Zod 4 skips object-level checks after an aborting child issue (an `invalid_type` anywhere in the dashboard, or an unrecognized key on the zod 4.4 line), so the refusal does not accompany such failures in one parse; the new test's "another key fails" case uses `columns: 99`, a continuable `max` check, which is why it holds. This is the same posture as #29162's array refine and every `superRefine` in the package, and the author gets the reserved-name issue on the next parse once the type error is fixed. Describe prose on `GlobalFilterSchema.name` and `globalFilters` says what the code now does and is regenerated at both reference sites. No finding.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.ui-dashboard-global-filter-reserved-date-range-refused.ts`** — against its first consumer (the generated registry, `os migrate meta`, the upgrade guide) and the sibling entry. `id` matches the changeset marker and the file name; `surface`, `replacement`, `reason` and `acceptanceCriteria` are filled in the sibling's register; `acceptanceCriteria` quotes the message's first sentence exactly as the test asserts it, so the guide and the door agree; the stored-row account (loads with `_diagnostics.valid: false`, next save refused, nothing rewrites) matches the "no conversion" stance and the dev's measured save-door behaviour; `conversionIds` and `relevantWhen` are omitted as in the sibling (both optional; `relevantWhen` is a reviewed addition enumerated by `semantic-relevance.test.ts`, and neither dashboard entry carries it). Not convertible is the right call: which of the two definitions the author meant is not derivable. No finding.

**Amended claim surface.** `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx` sentence: accurate (see should-fix 1). The ADR-0087 entry: judged above.

**Should-fix (non-blocking):**
1. `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx` keeps "the name `dateRange` is reserved for the built-in date range" unqualified immediately before the new sentence that says the key is refused only when `dateRange` is declared; the `GlobalFilterSchema.name` TSDoc says the key "is free" on a dashboard with no `dateRange`. A reader holds both. Qualifying the first sentence ("reserved for the built-in date range when the dashboard declares one") would make the prose say one thing. Prose only; the code is consistent.
2. Follow-up outside this PR's surface: `packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts` (`dashboard-filter-binding-unknown`, around line 408) says a `dateRange` binding key on a dashboard that declares no `dateRange` "is reported the same way: there is no date range for it to bind". With Q1 = A now written into the spec, that sentence is false when a `globalFilters` entry named `dateRange` exists (lint's own `dashboardFilterDefs` accepts the key then). Lint's file, not this claim's; worth a card so the explanation matches the ruling.

**Must-fix:** none.

## 待裁：新公开名字 `checkDashboardReservedDateRangeGlobalFilters`（#29213）

- 一句话问题：看板里一个全局筛选器占用 `dateRange` 这个 key 时，发布门会拒收，但 objectui 的编辑门原先放行，作者要到发布时才发现。修法是把这条检查导出成公开函数，让 objectui 镜像也挂上它。这个名字一旦发布就是公开契约。
